quiz.q: How does Plato resolve the philosophical conflict between Heraclitus and Parmenides regarding reality?
options: He rejects Parmenides entirely, arguing that ultimate truth constantly evolves within the changing physical realm.
He links change to the sensory physical world while assigning eternal permanence to the world of ideas.
He asserts that mathematical calculations prove physical matter is eternal while metaphysical ideas change continuously.
He follows Heraclitus in claiming that permanence is an illusion created by sensory perceptions of nature.
quiz.why: Plato synthesizes both thinkers by arguing that the physical world of appearances undergoes continuous change, whereas true ideas remain eternally permanent.

quiz.q: According to Socrates, how does genuine knowledge differ from the beliefs taught by the Sophists?
options: Genuine knowledge is inherent within the soul and discovered through dialectics, rather than bought for worldly gain.
Genuine knowledge consists of persuasive rhetorical techniques acquired by paying tuition fees to skilled political educators.
Genuine knowledge is derived from observing physical nature through inductive experiments rather than philosophical dialogue.
Genuine knowledge promotes aggressive individualism and material accumulation as the primary sources of human happiness.
quiz.why: Socrates argued that true knowledge is inherent in the soul and accessed through reasoned dialectics, whereas Sophists sold superficial opinions for material success.

quiz.q: What philosophical insight does Plato illustrate through the Allegory of the Cave regarding human understanding of reality?
options: Human beings possess innate physical senses capable of directly observing ultimate reality without philosophical training.
The physical world represents the highest truth, whereas abstract metaphysical ideas are mere cognitive illusions.
People in ignorance mistake changing physical appearances for true reality, which exists only as permanent ideas.
Enlightenment is achieved by studying empirical natural sciences rather than searching for spiritual essences beyond senses.
quiz.why: The allegory illustrates that people in ignorance mistake sensory appearances for reality, whereas true reality consists of permanent ideas beyond the physical realm.

quiz.q: Why does Plato's Theory of Ideas directly justify the political institution of the philosopher king?
options: Because philosophers alone possess the military courage required to defend the city against foreign Spartan armies.
Because philosophers accumulate extensive private property and material wealth to secure the economic stability of Athens.
Because democratic assemblies rely on dialectical debate to grant legislative legitimacy to elected philosophical rulers.
Because only philosophers possess the reason required to grasp the permanent idea of the ideal state.
quiz.why: Plato argued that establishing an ideal state requires understanding its eternal idea, which is only accessible through the reason possessed by philosophers.
